entry.title: Development :: RE: CamelForth for SG-1000 (RetroChallenge 2026/10)
entry.dc:creator: leadedsolder
entry.dc:subject: Development
entry.content:
Author: leadedsolder
Posted: Sun Nov 01, 2026 4:45 pm (GMT 0)

I'm not going to deny that it's hard to read, but it's surprisingly fluent to write. If you're used to the "pipe" operator in ML or Haskell, or even just partial application in FP, there's a comforting amount of overlap. I wonder if Japanese folks have an easier time with the syntax, too.

Thanks for the nice words! I'm not sure where this project will go next, but I'm putting it on the shelf for a bit to go back to other projects.

entry.dc:subject: Music
entry.content:
Author: Splats
Posted: Sun Nov 01, 2026 2:15 pm (GMT 0)

Maxim wrote
We tend to ignore Brazil and Korea in favour of Japan, USA and Europe for “where was it released”.


Yeah, that makes sense. At the time, the latter three regions were the "main" gaming territories, while gamers elsewhere mostly had bootlegs and rebranded versions like the Samsung Gam*Boy.

And man, I didn't think this thread would get so in-depth, but it's for the best. Sometimes, mistakes can stick because nobody bothers to correct them, especially with ancient video games.
